id.description: The user, token, automation or add-on; empty for Racksail itself

impersonator.description: Who was viewing the panel as the person

impersonatorName.description: The username of whoever was viewing the panel as them, as it was then

name.description: Its name: a username, a token's or an add-on's name

source.description: The surface it came through: the panel's pages, the racksail command, the API and so on

type.description: What acted: a person, an API token, an automation, an add-on, the assistant or Racksail itself

user.description: The person responsible, when something acted for them

userName.description: The username of the person responsible, as it was then

apiVersion.description: The hook API version the add-on speaks, such as v1

status.description: ok when the add-on can take hook calls

actor.description: Who made it, and what acted for them

changedSince.description: For an undo, the resources that changed after the change set it undoes: undoing puts back their settings from before that change set all the same, so what changed since goes too

changes.description: Its changes, in the order they are planned and applied

conflicts.description: Fields two contributors change; a change set with any can't be applied

contributions.description: What hooks and add-ons added to it, and who they are

dryRun.description: Whether it is a preview, which changes nothing until it is applied

effects.description: What applying it does to the machine: downloads, packages, ports, services, files and the rest

estimate.description: What applying it costs, all told

id.description: The change set's ID, which starts with chg_

job.description: The job that carries out its changes on the machine

risk.description: How much harm applying it can do: the highest risk of its changes

snapshot.description: Whether it removes data, so read-only snapshots are taken first of what holds it

snapshots.description: The snapshots taken before it was applied, which a restore brings data back from

state.description: Where it is: planned, being applied, applied, failed or undone

title.description: What the change set does, in a few words

undoOf.description: The change set it undoes, when it is an undo

message.description: What the conflict is, in English

resource.description: The resource whose field two contributors change

changes.description: The changes they added or rewrote, as indexes into the change set's changes

effects.description: The effects they added, as indexes into the change set's effects

action.description: What happens, for example install, open, start or write

contributor.description: Who added this effect when it wasn't the requested change itself

detail.description: Extra detail such as a version

target.description: What changes: a package, a port such as tcp/443, a unit or a path

type.description: What kind of change this is

diskBytes.description: How much more disk it takes, in bytes

downloadBytes.description: How much applying it downloads, in bytes

memoryBytes.description: How much more memory what it runs takes, in bytes

op.description: Whether the field was added, removed or replaced

path.description: The field, with dots and indexes, such as domains[0]

sensitive.description: Whether the field holds a secret, whose values the diff leaves out

params.description: The values the code's message is filled in with

value.description: The offending value, when it's safe to show

expect.description: The expected status code, unit state, address or certificate name

name.description: What the check confirms, such as the site answering

target.description: A URL, host:port, unit name or DNS name

timeout.description: How long the check keeps trying, in nanoseconds

actor.description: Who is making the change, and through what

change.description: Validate hooks: the index of the change to decide on

changeSet.description: The change set, at points of the change pipeline

changes.description: Modify and observe hooks: the indexes of the changes the point is about

config.description: System hooks: the configuration to patch

data.description: What happened, at lifecycle and identity points

point.description: The hook point, such as web.site.create.validate

changeSet.description: Modify hooks: the change set with the hook's changes, which may be new specs for the changes the point is about, added changes and added effects. A reply that changes anything else counts as a failure of the hook

reason.description: Why the change is refused, shown to the person making it

input.description: Its input, checked against the action's JSON Schema

name.description: The action, as the kind declares it

status.description: The kind's own status fields, as its status schema describes them

action.description: Set to plan or apply an action of the resource rather than its settings

dir.description: The only directory the plan's steps may touch, which the add-on can read

results.description: Apply: what each step of the plan returned

effects.description: What applying does beyond the steps, such as records it makes with an outside service, for the preview

spec.description: Actions: the resource's new settings, when the action changes them

steps.description: Agent operations to run on the server: WriteFile, EnsureDir, RemovePath, ReadFile, StatPath and ListDir, of paths in dir

deleted.description: Set while it is deleted: the plan removes what earlier plans wrote, and applying undoes what the add-on did for it

generation.description: Its generation, which goes up whenever its settings change

kind.description: Its kind, one the add-on adds

spec.description: Its settings, as the kind's JSON Schema describes them

status.description: Its status: what the add-on last reported, with the phase and conditions the panel keeps

code.description: Stable error code in the form <module>.<snake_case>

examples: The domain example.com is already used by another site.

instance.description: A URI reference for this occurrence

params.description: Values for the placeholders in the code's message

title.description: Short summary of the problem type

type.description: A URI reference for the problem type

input.description: What the method takes, as the capability's interface describes it

action.description: The action taken, when the change is one

after.description: Its settings after the change; secret fields hold references, never values

before.description: Its settings before the change, which undoing it puts back; secret fields hold references, never values

checks.description: What confirms an action's steps worked, once they have run

diff.description: What the change does to each field of the settings

id.description: The resource the change is about

labels.description: The resource's labels after the change

labelsBefore.description: Its labels before the change, which undoing it puts back

op.description: What the change does: creates, updates or deletes the resource, or takes one of its actions

output.description: What the action returned, once it was applied

revision.description: The revision of the resource the change was planned against

server.description: The cluster server the resource is placed on; empty for the panel's own server

source.description: Who asked for the change: the request, or the hook or add-on that added it

state.description: How far carrying out the change got: started while it runs or after it failed, done once it is in place; empty until it starts

steps.description: The agent operations an action runs on the machine, besides what applying the resource does

changed.description: Whether anything changed, or in check mode would change

id.description: The owning reseller or account; empty for server-wide resources

hook.description: The hook point the contribution came through

name.description: Which contributor it was, such as an add-on's id and version

type.description: Who contributed it: the request itself, a hook, a rule, an add-on or a module

title.description: What the step does, for progress logs

info.description: What an add-on serves on its Unix socket for the panel: its health, its hooks, the capabilities it provides, the plans and applies of the kinds it adds, and its routes and screens. Hooks answer within their deadline; an error or a timeout counts as a failure, which blocks the change only for hooks whose failure mode is block. The panel never sends data the add-on's permissions don't grant.
info.title: Racksail add-on protocol

get.description: The panel calls it after starting the add-on and from its health checks.
get.summary: Check that the add-on is running

post.description: Validate hooks allow or deny one change, modify hooks return the change set with their changes, observe hooks only take note, and system hooks return the patched configuration.

parameters.description: The hook point, as in the call
parameters.name: point

post.summary: Run one of the add-on's hooks

post.description: The panel calls it once the plan's steps have run, with what they returned. The add-on does what the plan said it would besides, and answers with the resource's status, or with a problem, which fails the change. For a resource being deleted, it undoes what it did for it.

parameters.description: The kind, one the add-on's manifest adds, such as guard.rule
parameters.name: kind

200.description: The resource's status, and an action's output

post.summary: Apply a resource of a kind the add-on adds

post.description: The panel calls it as it plans a change of the resource, or one of its actions, for the preview and again to apply it, and when it puts back what drifted. The plan is the steps the agent runs, only of files in dir, and what applying does beyond them. Planning changes nothing, and the same call always gets the same plan.

parameters.description: The kind, one the add-on's manifest adds, such as guard.rule
parameters.name: kind

post.summary: Plan a resource of a kind the add-on adds

post.description: The panel calls it when it uses a capability the add-on declares under provides, such as sending a notification for notifier or creating a record for dns. The capability's interface says what each method takes and returns.

parameters.description: The capability, as under provides

parameters.description: The method, such as send
parameters.name: method

post.summary: Call a method of a capability the add-on provides

The panel shows them in a sandboxed frame of an origin of their own, so they can never read the panel's session; the frame's address signs in what its page loads and asks for under it, as the person who opened it.
